Defines beta_nu as the maximum of the last Smith invariant d_s(C) over nonsingular binary matrices of every size at most nu. The repository deliberately avoids a single numeral-valued beta: `BinaryBeta.BetaBound N B` and `BetaAttained N B` are the upper and lower halves as predicates (packaged as `BetaExact N B`), with d_s(C) rendered as `SharpClearing.inverseDenominator` -- the lcm of the denominators of the rational inverse -- and identified with the final Smith factor of any `SmithWitness` by `inverseDenominator_eq_smithLastFactor`. `BetaExists.betaOf N` is the literal supremum, `sup_{s <= N} betaAt s` with `betaAt s` the sup of `inverseDenominator` over zero-one s x s matrices, and satisfies `betaBound_betaOf`; it differs from the display only by also ranging over s = 0 and over singular C, both of which contribute the value 1. | ADVERSARIAL CHECK: All eight read. `BetaBound N B` (BinaryBeta.lean:30) quantifies over `1 <= s <= N` and zero-one `C : Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) Z` with `C.det != 0`, concluding `inverseDenominator C <= B` -- the display's max as an upper-bound predicate; `BetaAttained` (line 36) is the matching existential and `BetaExact` (line 44) the structure pairing them. `SharpClearing.inverseDenominator` (line 41) is `Denominator.lcmDen (inverseEntries C)`, the lcm of denominators of Mathlib's rational inverse, and `inverseDenominator_eq_smithLastFactor` (line 525) proves it equals `w.lastFactor` for any `SmithWitness C`, which is the display's d_s(C). `BetaExists.betaAt s` (line 45) is the sup over `Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) Bool`, `betaOf N` (line 57) the sup over `Finset.range (N+1)`, and `betaBound_betaOf` (line 65) gives `BetaBound N (betaOf N)`. The review's caveat is right: betaOf also ranges over s = 0 and over singular C, where the empty/zero inverse makes `inverseDenominator = 1` (`inverseDenominator_pos` plus `lcmDen` of an all-integer family). `definition` is the right kind.

Lean subtracts the reference sector's phase explicitly where the manuscript normalizes phi_1 away by giving the rows for x in T_1 a zero colour block (`colorRow_base`); `color_dot_realUnknown` is the resulting colour-block dot product. | ADVERSARIAL CHECK: Read all three. `realUnknown` (FiniteLift.lean:230) is `Sum (Fin n) (Color D) -> R` with `Sum.inl j |-> theta j` and `Sum.inr g |-> -(D.phase g.1 - D.phase (baseSector D))` -- literally the display, with `Color D = {alpha // alpha != baseSector D}` supplying the ell - 1 relative-phase coordinates. `baseSector D` (line 84) is sector 0. `color_dot_realUnknown` (line 235) proves the colour-block dot product equals `-(D.phase alpha - D.phase (baseSector D))`, and `colorRow_base` (line 213) is the zero colour block on the reference sector, which is the review's point about how Lean normalizes phi_1 away. `definition` is right.
